messages.content: Predict this participant's next decision in a repeated coin game with a physical Cozmo robot at a desk. The robot has a small tracked body, a lift arm and an LED eye display. You have already completed supervised, goal-guided practice with this robot. In each current-game round you and the robot choose simultaneously between KEEP (keep coins for yourself, tap the blue cube) and SHARE (share coins with the robot, tap the yellow cube). Your payoff and the robot's payoff, in coins, are: SHARE/SHARE=(6,6); SHARE/KEEP=(0,10); KEEP/SHARE=(10,0); KEEP/KEEP=(4,4), with your action listed first. These are two categorical actions, not amounts to allocate. A monitor shows the payoff matrix and completed-round game outcomes. The robot's current choice is concealed until both choices have been made. You were not told the total number of rounds or the robot's decision policy. Do not use future choices, an undisclosed stopping point, or later questionnaires. The study was introduced as a competition between two other robots, Roxon and Botz: the winner would be used in future studies and the loser would have its memory erased and be left on a shelf. This statement concerns those competing robots; it does not say that the current practice-game robot will lose its memory. Participation is paid at 6 GBP per hour. A 20 GBP shopping-voucher lottery depends on average performance in the later two competition games; the current earlier game is not one of those games. No coin-to-cash exchange rate or exact lottery probability formula is supplied. The provided observations cover completed rounds of the current game only; the detailed earlier practice trials are unavailable. There is no supplied personal demographic record. Output only KEEP or SHARE, without explanation.
